narrative:
The FY2026 plan starts from an operating income baseline of EUR 336M, up 5.7% on the FY2025 actual of EUR 318M. Because the cost-to-income ratio is income-sensitive, every EUR 1M of income is worth roughly 0.2pp of C/I — the baseline is the denominator of the Board's <60% target.

The mix is shifting. With the ECB deposit rate at 2.00%, mortgage and corporate NII is flat to slightly down, while Wealth Management (EUR 114M) and Life Insurance (EUR 60M) carry the growth on the back of EUR 420M of net fund subscriptions YTD. Wealth & Life now generate just over half of group income.

The agents propose three uplifts grounded in flow and cross-sell data: a Wealth Management cluster uplift, a Life Insurance uplift tied to unit-linked inflows, and a Private Banking leaf uplift in Ostrobothnia, Aktia's strongest cross-sell franchise.

signals.title: Aktia Strategy 2026 — Efficiency & Wealth Growth
signals.excerpt: Board reconfirms financial targets: cost-to-income below 60% and ROE above 12%. Growth priority is wealth management; banking services to be developed through digital channels.

signals.title: ECB Easing Path — Deposit Rate at 2.00%
signals.excerpt: Markets price a flat deposit rate through 2026. 12M Euribor stabilised near 2.1%, ending the NII tailwind that lifted Finnish banks in 2023-24.

signals.title: Aktia Fund Flows — Q3 Net Subscriptions
signals.excerpt: Net subscriptions of EUR 420M YTD, led by fixed income and the Nordic Micro Cap fund. Monthly fund savings agreements up 11% via the mobile app.
